expectations.note: With playback active and browsing /opt/nothingness, the accessible jump-to-now-playing-folder action was present; activation navigated to /opt/nothingness/media and the playing track was visible in the resulting browser state.

In /opt/nothingness/media, the playing 06-undercover-54 track was off-screen at scrollPosition 151.6 while the labeled track action was present; activating it kept currentPath unchanged and brought row 54 into the viewport at scrollPosition 0.0.
After the jump, row 54 was fully within the browser viewport (Rect y 143.8-184.8 at scrollPosition 0.0), but the semantics tree still exposed the active 'jump to now-playing track' action.
A live verification captured isPlaying false and songInfo null, and its semantics tree contained no jump action label.
The active action was discoverable in the semantics tree with the distinguishing label 'jump to now-playing track' and tap action.
The candidate captured a genuine before PNG with the browser collapsed and the playing track absent; the live pre-jump verification likewise shows the off-screen row and active action.
The candidate's genuine after PNG shows rows through 54 in the same /opt/nothingness/media folder; the live post-jump screenshot and semantics show row 54 visible after activation.

The candidate's drive replay recorded playback, folder state, activation, and before/after screenshots, but it did not capture its claimed accessibility semantics or explicitly verify the same-folder scrolled case in its own session; those claims required the judge's live re-check.

An actual on-screen folder-row tap navigated into /opt/nothingness/media, and pause/resume remained responsive; next/previous had no queued track to transition to, so the full playback-control sweep was not demonstrated.
Repeated jump activations and live inspection left the app responsive; runtime overflow reports remained empty and no feature-attributable crash surfaced.
